plan: [I have value $39. Assuming other bidders bid their private values (naive/neutral model), if I bid b I win with probability (b/49)^4 and, conditional on winning, expect to pay 0.6b (the 2nd-highest of the other four). Expected payoff ~ (b/49)^4(39 - 0.6b), maximized at b ≥ 4·39/3 = 52, so constrained optimum is at the upper bound. To secure the win and maximize expected profit, bid the maximum feasible common-range amount: $49.]

[Symmetric equilibrium for a 3rd-price auction with n=5 and uniform values is linear. Using b(v)=a·v and solving the FOC yields a=4/3. Thus the optimal bid is b(v)=4/3·v. With my private value $27, the equilibrium bid is 4/3*27 = $36. This maximizes expected profit for the single round.]

[Assume other bidders follow the symmetric behavior for a 3rd-price auction with 5 bidders. If others bid their values, my expected profit as a function of my bid b is (b/49)^4*(v-0.6b). Maximizing that yields b = 4v/3 ≈ 17.333. This overbids relative to value but optimally trades off win probability and expected third-price payment. I'll bid 17.3 (nearest $0.1).]

[Because this is a third-price auction (winner pays the third-highest bid) and values are iid, bidding aggressively raises winning probability while payment depends on others' bids, not my own. With value $42 and no reliable history, the robust profit-maximizing approach is to bid the maximum allowed to maximize chance of winning while expected third-price typically stays below my value. I therefore place the top feasible bid.]

[This is a one-shot third-price auction with 4 opponents and v=39. Winning yields profit v − (third-highest bid). Overbidding increases win probability without changing the paid price when I become highest, but risks winning when the third price exceeds my value. With no history and uniform unknown opponents, a conservative truthful bid avoids systematically paying more than my value and serves as a robust baseline that maximizes expected long-run profit under uncertainty. I therefore bid my value: $39.]
